servers.name: doe-research
servers.description: Literature, datasets, software, and discovery over OSTI's four public APIs, DOE's rulemakings from the Federal Register, the laboratories' patents and released software, plus the source registry and a cross-catalog fan-out.

tools.name: research.search_literature
tools.description: Search DOE-funded research literature — technical reports, journal articles, conference papers, patents, theses — across OSTI.GOV (4.4M records) and DOE PAGES (260K public-access records) at once, deduplicated by DOI. Use for any question about published DOE or national-laboratory research. Filter by topic (query), author, research_org (the lab that did the work), sponsor_org (the office that paid), or a year range. Set public_access_only to restrict to work whose full text DOE guarantees — but note DOE PAGES applies a 12-month embargo, so recent papers are systematically absent from it. Read coverage.pagination: total_matches is often far larger than what one call returns, and reporting the page as the answer would be wrong by orders of magnitude.

tools.name: research.search_datasets
tools.description: Search DOE Data Explorer (1.03M records) for DOE-funded research DATASETS. Returns metadata, DOIs, and landing pages — never the data, which lives at national labs, user facilities, and universities. Use when the user wants data rather than papers, or wants a dataset's DOI to cite. site_code filters to one repository (DOE-GDR returns the Geothermal Data Repository's 1,035 registered submissions, which is the only API route into it). For raw user-facility experimental data — beamline shots, reactor runs — expect nothing: that is proposal-gated by design, not a gap.

tools.name: research.search_software
tools.description: Search DOE CODE (7,675 records) for DOE-funded software: repository links, licences, developers with ORCIDs, and sponsoring organizations. Use for 'what DOE-funded tool does X'. Filter by language or developer; set open_source_only to exclude closed-source records, which carry no repository link by classification rather than by omission. Registration is voluntary, so absence is not proof the software does not exist.

tools.name: research.get_record
tools.description: Fetch one full record by id from a named OSTI collection: 'literature' (OSTI.GOV), 'pages' (DOE PAGES), 'dataset' (DOE Data Explorer), or 'software' (DOE CODE). The collections have SEPARATE id spaces — the same number is a different record in each — so pass the collection the id came from rather than guessing. The answer includes a `fulltext` block saying whether the work can actually be read and where — the OSTI full-text URL when one exists, the DOI as a fallback to the publisher otherwise. No full-text link is NOT a paywall finding; it means OSTI exposes none.

tools.name: registry.resolve_org
tools.description: Resolve a DOE organization from a name, abbreviation, FORMER name, or domain — including dead ones. Use FIRST whenever a user names a lab or office, because this ecosystem renames things and the old URLs do not redirect. 'NREL' resolves to the National Laboratory of the Rockies and warns that the name is historical; a *.nrel.gov domain resolves the same way and warns that the URL is dead with no forwarding. Same for EERE (now CMEI), FECM (now HGEO), LPO (now EDF), HFTO and BETO (merged into AFFO), IEDO (now ITO), and the dismantled Grid Deployment Office.

tools.name: registry.lab_crosswalk
tools.description: What a DOE national laboratory publishes, across every platform carrying its data. Call with no argument for all seventeen labs and their source counts. Servers here are organized by data domain, not by laboratory, so this is how a lab-oriented question gets answered — and it is the honest way, since several labs' flagship data lives on shared cross-lab platforms rather than their own domains. A lab with zero sources is a gap in this project, not a claim that the lab publishes nothing.

tools.name: discovery.search_all_catalogs
tools.description: Search four DOE dataset catalogs at once — DOE Data Explorer, ORNL's Open Energy Data Hub, energy.gov/data.json, and energy.gov/code.json — labelling each result with its catalog and that catalog's vintage. Use when the user is looking for a dataset and does not know which DOE system holds it. The catalogs overlap and disagree, and two of them are measurably stale: data.json holds entries last touched in 2014 beside current ones. Weigh the vintage rather than treating all four as equally current.

tools.name: discovery.list_pure_resources
tools.description: DOE's seven designated Public Reusable Research (PuRe) data resources — the department's own list of its most durable public data holdings: ATcT, Materials Project, ARM, JGI, KBase, the Particle Data Group, and NNDC. Use when a user asks what DOE considers its flagship public data, or wants an authoritative starting point for a scientific domain.

tools.name: docs.search_rulemakings
tools.description: DOE's rules, proposed rules, and notices as published in the Federal Register: the official text, with docket id, CFR parts, regulatory identifier, and a full-text link on every record. `query` is full-text; `document_type` takes NOTICE, PRESDOCU, PRORULE, RULE (comma-separated); `docket`, `since` and `until` (YYYY-MM-DD) narrow further. FERC is filed under DOE in this API and is out of DOE-MCP's scope, so its documents are dropped and the count of dropped ones rides on the answer. Comments and docket material are NOT here.

tools.name: docs.get_rulemaking
tools.description: One Federal Register document in full by its document number, in the publisher's own form ('2026-17979'). Returns the same fields as docs.search_rulemakings for a single record. A document belonging to an agency DOE-MCP does not cover is reported as found but not served, with coverage.registry='none' rather than as a miss.

tools.name: tech.find_licensable_ip
tools.description: Patents held and software released by the US national laboratories, from PNNL's technology-transfer index — the one place a single laboratory's own output is searchable. Use for 'what has Idaho patented on X', 'what software has PNNL released', 'who invented this'. `lab` takes an acronym or a laboratory name and is resolved against the alias table first, because this service answers an unknown acronym with zero results and no error. `record_type` is Patent or Software; `query`, `inventor`, `taxonomy`, `since` and `until` narrow further. Pass `record_id` for one record whole, including the filed patent text a search page omits. Page with `cursor` ALONE — filters sent with a cursor are ignored by the service. Being listed is not an offer to license.

servers.name: doe-energy-data
servers.description: EIA's self-describing statistics tree, BPA's five-minute grid feed, the USGS/LBNL wind and solar facility inventories, and the DOE/EPA vehicle fuel-economy service.

tools.name: energy.discover_routes
tools.description: Walk EIA's self-describing route tree to find the dataset that answers a question. Call with no route for the top level (electricity, natural-gas, petroleum, coal, nuclear-outages, international...), then with a child id to descend. A leaf route returns its frequencies, facets, data columns, and period range — everything energy.get_data needs. ALWAYS walk here first: EIA returns empty rows rather than an error for a wrong column name.

tools.name: energy.get_data
tools.description: Rows from a named EIA dataset route. Pass data_columns as a comma-separated list of exact column names from energy.discover_routes, and facets as 'name=v1,v2;other=v3'. EIA caps responses at 5,000 rows; when coverage.pagination says truncated, page with offset rather than describing what you got as the whole series. Needs an EIA API key — EIA's own, not an api.data.gov key.

tools.name: energy.grid_status
tools.description: Recent hourly electricity data for a US balancing authority from EIA-930 (CISO, ERCO, PJM, MISO, ISNE, NYIS, BPAT...). Use for 'how much power did X use'. `metric` picks one of four measurements that share this route: demand (the default, and what 'how much power did X use' means), forecast (day-ahead, and its newest hours have NOT happened yet), generation, or interchange. Recent hours are PRELIMINARY and get revised, so this is operational reporting rather than settled statistics — the envelope says so on every answer.

tools.name: grid.get_bpa_operations
tools.description: Near-live load and generation inside the Bonneville Power Administration balancing authority, at five-minute resolution over a rolling seven-day window: load, VER (wind and solar), hydro, fossil/biomass, nuclear, and net interchange. `intervals` is how many of the most recent five-minute readings to return; 12 is the last hour. This is the Pacific Northwest at five-minute resolution — for any other balancing authority, or for hourly history, use energy.grid_status.

tools.name: fuel.find_vehicle
tools.description: Official EPA fuel-economy ratings for US-market vehicles, 1984 onward. A strict drill-down: call with no arguments for years, then year for makes, then year+make for models, then year+make+model for trim options whose values are vehicle ids. Call with vehicle_id for the full record — ratings, tailpipe CO2, electric range, annual fuel cost. These are test-cycle values, not real-world consumption.

tools.name: fuel.get_prices
tools.description: Current US national average fuel prices by type: regular, midgrade, premium, diesel, E85, CNG, LPG, and electricity. One current figure each, no history and no regional breakdown — for those use energy.get_data against EIA's petroleum routes.

tools.name: facility.find_wind_turbines
tools.description: Where individual US wind turbines are and what they are, from the USGS/LBNL wind turbine database: state, county, project name, manufacturer, model, rated capacity, hub height, rotor diameter, year, and coordinates, land-based and offshore. Filter by `state` (two-letter), `county`, `project`, a `bbox` of minlon,minlat,maxlon,maxlat, or `filters` in the publisher's own form, 'p_year=gte.2020;t_cap=gt.3000', semicolon-separated. An inventory, NOT generation: for output use energy.get_data. Every row carries confidence codes, and the answer says how many are below full confidence.

tools.name: facility.find_solar_facilities
tools.description: Where US utility-scale solar facilities of one megawatt and up are and what they are, from the USGS/LBNL photovoltaic database: state, county, facility name, AC and DC capacity, panel technology, axis type, tilt, site type, agrivoltaic status, year, power region, and coordinates. Same filter arguments as facility.find_wind_turbines, against this table's columns ('p_cap_ac=gt.100;p_axis=eq.single-axis'). Rooftop and community solar are not in it. An inventory, not generation.

tools.description: Resolve a DOE organization from a name, abbreviation, FORMER name, or domain — including dead ones. Use FIRST whenever a user names a lab or office, because this ecosystem renames things and the old URLs do not redirect. 'NREL' resolves to the National Laboratory of the Rockies and warns that the name is historical; a *.nrel.gov domain resolves the same way and warns that the URL is dead with no forwarding. servers.name: doe-energy-tech
servers.description: What is modelled, tested or published for an energy technology: the NLR developer network (PVWatts, solar resource, tariffs, alternative-fuel stations), the ATB and Cambium releases, module and battery test data, and the geothermal, marine, hydropower, bioenergy and carbon-storage repositories. Holds the api.data.gov and EDX keys; nothing in it is built yet.

servers.name: doe-earth
servers.description: Daymet single-pixel weather from ORNL DAAC, ESS-DIVE's environmental datasets, the ESGF climate-model index, and the Sage/Waggle sensor-node inventory.

tools.name: earth.get_daymet_point
tools.description: Daily surface weather for one point in North America, Hawaii, or Puerto Rico, 1980 onward, from ORNL DAAC's Daymet: maximum and minimum temperature, precipitation, shortwave radiation, snow water equivalent, vapour pressure, and day length. `variables` is a comma-separated list (default all); `start` and `end` are ISO dates spanning at most 3660 days. These are MODELLED values for the 1 km cell containing the point, interpolated from ground stations — not a station observation. Daymet's year is 365 days long: 29 February is kept and 31 December is dropped, and the answer names any such date inside the range.

tools.name: earth.search_datasets
tools.description: Search ESS-DIVE, DOE's repository for environmental system science data: terrestrial ecosystem, watershed, and subsurface biogeochemistry studies, including NGEE Arctic and Tropics, SPRUCE, and the integrated field laboratories. `text` searches the whole record; `keywords` matches the depositor's own keyword list and is much narrower; `creator` is an author name; `project` is the field laboratory or campaign. Returns metadata and landing pages, not data files. For one record in full use earth.get_dataset.

tools.name: earth.get_dataset
tools.description: One ESS-DIVE dataset in full by its package id, which comes from earth.search_datasets: creators and their ORCIDs, funding programme, licence, keywords, the methods the depositor described, the places and period it covers, and its citation. The data files themselves are reached through the landing page in access_recipes.

tools.name: climate.discover_facets
tools.description: Walk the ESGF climate-model index before searching it. Call with no argument for the searchable facets it publishes; call with `facet` set to one of them — source_id, experiment_id, variable_id, frequency, nominal_resolution — for the values it takes and how many datasets carry each. ALWAYS walk here first: the archive holds millions of datasets under controlled vocabularies, and a model or variable name that is nearly right returns nothing at all rather than a suggestion.

tools.name: climate.search_cmip
tools.description: Find climate-model output in the ESGF index: which model ran which experiment for which variable, at what frequency and resolution, over what period, and which data node holds the files. `model`, `experiment`, `variable`, `frequency`, and `institution` are the named facets; `filters` takes any other as 'grid_label=gn;realm=atmos'. Values must be exact — walk climate.discover_facets first. Returns the latest version of each dataset by default because the index holds retracted and superseded output and sorts it first otherwise. Metadata only; the output lives on federated data nodes, some of which need a federation account.

tools.name: sensors.find_nodes
tools.description: Where the Sage/Waggle edge-sensor network's nodes are and what is on them: deployment phase, project, host address, coordinates, onboard computers, and instruments — cameras, weather and air-quality packages, microphones, rain gauges, lidar. Filter by `vsn` (the node's call sign, like W08D), `project`, `phase`, or `instrument`, or pass `latitude`/`longitude` with an optional `within_km` for the nearest ones. An INVENTORY, not measurements: the readings are a separate service and the answer says how to reach it.

tools.description: Resolve a DOE organization from a name, abbreviation, FORMER name, or domain — including dead ones. servers.name: doe-materials
servers.description: The Materials Project's keyless OPTIMADE endpoint for computed inorganic structures, and the Basis Set Exchange for quantum-chemistry basis sets.

tools.name: materials.describe_structure_fields
tools.description: Which properties the Materials Project's OPTIMADE endpoint can be filtered on, with the provider's own description of each and its extension fields marked — `_mp_stability` carries formation energy and energy above hull, which the standard does not define. ALWAYS walk here before writing a filter for materials.search_structures: a property this provider does not have is refused rather than ignored, and the extension fields are the ones nobody guesses.

tools.name: materials.search_structures
tools.description: Find computed inorganic crystal structures in the Materials Project by composition. `elements` is a comma-separated list every result must contain ('Ga,N'); `formula` is an exact reduced formula ('GaN'); `nelements` is a count with an optional operator ('2', '<=3'); `filter` takes the OPTIMADE grammar directly for anything else. Returns structures and formulas — COMPUTED, not measured. This keyless route does not carry the energetics, electronic structure, or phase diagrams behind the Materials Project's own keyed API.

tools.name: materials.get_structure
tools.description: One computed structure in full by its id, which comes from materials.search_structures and looks like 'mp-1244984': formulas, elements and their ratios, site count, lattice vectors, space group, and the provider's own fields including its stability block.

tools.name: chemistry.search_basis_sets
tools.description: Find quantum-chemistry basis sets in the Basis Set Exchange, which originated at PNNL/EMSL and is run with MolSSI. `query` matches name, description and alternative names; `family` is the lineage (pople, dunning, ahlrichs, karlsruhe...); `role` is what the set is for (orbital, jkfit, rifit...); `covers_elements` takes symbols or atomic numbers and keeps only sets defined for ALL of them — the way to answer 'which basis sets cover uranium'. Returns the keys chemistry.get_basis_set takes.

tools.name: chemistry.get_basis_set
tools.description: One basis set rendered as a named program's own input text, ready to paste into a calculation: NWChem, Gaussian, Psi4, ORCA, Molpro, CP2K and twenty more. `name` is a key or name from chemistry.search_basis_sets; `elements` narrows it to the ones you need, as symbols or atomic numbers. The citations for the set come back with it — the publisher asks that sets be cited and they live at a different endpoint from the data.

tools.name: registry.resolve_org
tools.description: Resolve a DOE organization from a name, abbreviation, FORMER name, or domain — including dead ones. Use FIRST whenever a user names a lab or office, because this ecosystem renames things and the old URLs do not redirect. servers.name: doe-nuclear
servers.description: Nuclide structure and decay data. The ingest-versus-wrap question is deliberately still open.

servers.name: doe-bio
servers.description: Microbiome studies and biosamples; JGI and EMSL as pointer tools.

servers.name: doe-projects
servers.description: ARPA-E awards, the loan portfolio, the Lab Partnering Service. VIPS did not wait for it: the laboratories' patents and software ship in doe-research as tech.find_licensable_ip.

servers.name: doe-docs
servers.description: NEPA documents and DOE directives — or a catalog entry pointing at PNNL's NEPA-MCP, which already serves them. The Federal Register slice did not wait for it: it needs no crawler and ships in doe-research as docs.search_rulemakings and docs.get_rulemaking.

sources.name: Sage / Waggle edge sensor network
sources.scope: Every node in the Sage/Waggle network with its deployment phase, project, coordinates, host address, computers, and instruments — cameras, weather and air-quality packages, microphones, rain gauges, and lidar.

sources.name: Basis Set Exchange
sources.scope: Quantum-chemistry basis sets by name, element, and program format (NWChem, Gaussian, CP2K, and thirty others), with the metadata and literature references for each set.

sources.name: BPA transmission operations feeds
sources.scope: Near-live load and generation inside the Bonneville Power Administration balancing authority at five-minute resolution over a rolling seven-day window: load, VER (variable energy resources — wind and solar), hydro, fossil/biomass, and nuclear, with net interchange on the second feed. Values are megawatts from BPA's own SCADA system.

sources.name: DOE Software Inventory (code.json)
sources.steward: Office of the Chief Information Officer
sources.scope: DOE's declared inventory of software releases across the department and its laboratories: name, description, repository URL, licence permissions, languages, and organization.

sources.name: DOE-MCP source registry and organization table
sources.scope: Which public DOE systems this project knows about, who stewards and funds each one, what its terms say, what it does not cover, and what is blocking the ones that are not wired up. Plus the organization table with the alias sets that resolve former names and dead domains.

sources.name: DOE Open Data Catalog (data.json)
sources.steward: Office of the Chief Information Officer
sources.scope: DOE's declared inventory of public datasets across program offices, in the federal Project Open Data format.

sources.name: DOE PuRe Data Resources directory
sources.scope: The seven resources DOE's Office of Science designates as Public Reusable Research data resources, each with this project's own status against it.

sources.name: EIA API v2
sources.scope: US energy statistics as a self-describing tree: electricity (including EIA-930 hourly demand, generation and interchange by balancing authority), natural gas, petroleum, coal, nuclear outages, renewables, international, and more.

sources.name: ESGF search (CMIP6)
sources.scope: Metadata for climate-model output published through the Earth System Grid Federation, CMIP6 above all: which model ran which experiment for which variable, at what frequency and resolution, over what period, and which data node holds the files.

sources.name: ESS-DIVE (Environmental System Science Data Infrastructure)
sources.scope: Data from DOE's environmental system science programme: terrestrial ecosystem, watershed, and subsurface biogeochemistry studies, including the NGEE Arctic and Tropics campaigns, SPRUCE, and the integrated field laboratories.

sources.name: Federal Register API (Department of Energy documents)
sources.steward: Office of the Federal Register (National Archives)
sources.scope: Rules, proposed rules, notices, and presidential documents published by DOE and its component agencies, with docket ids, CFR references, regulatory identifiers, and links to the full text. FERC's documents are excluded by scope, not by the publisher.

sources.name: fueleconomy.gov web service
sources.scope: Official EPA fuel-economy ratings for US-market vehicles from 1984 onward, roughly 140 fields per vehicle including city/highway/combined ratings, tailpipe CO2, electric range and consumption for EVs and PHEVs, and annual fuel cost. Plus current national average fuel prices by fuel type.

sources.name: Materials Project OPTIMADE endpoint
sources.scope: Crystal structures of inorganic materials as the OPTIMADE standard describes them: elements and their ratios, reduced, descriptive and Hill formulas, site count, lattice vectors, space group, and dimensionality, plus the Materials Project's own stability fields.

sources.name: ORNL DAAC (Daymet, MODIS/VIIRS subsets)
sources.scope: Biogeochemical and ecological data, including Daymet daily surface weather for North America — queryable one pixel at a time, which is the rare bulk-science case with a genuine subsetting service — and MODIS/VIIRS land-product subsets, which are not wired up.

sources.name: Open Energy Data Hub (ORNL)
sources.scope: ORNL-hosted energy datasets across transportation electrification, grid, and buildings, including EV Watts and ARPA-E PERFORM.

sources.name: DOE Data Explorer
sources.steward: Office of Scientific and Technical Information
sources.scope: Metadata and DOIs for DOE-funded research datasets held at national laboratories, user facilities, universities, and other repositories. Discovery layer only: DDE hosts no data.

sources.name: DOE CODE
sources.steward: Office of Scientific and Technical Information
sources.scope: DOE-funded scientific and business software: open-source projects with repository links, and closed-source project metadata. Licences, developers with ORCIDs, sponsoring organizations, and DOIs.

sources.name: DOE PAGES (Public Access Gateway for Energy and Science)
sources.steward: Office of Scientific and Technical Information
sources.scope: Peer-reviewed scholarly publications resulting from DOE funding, with full text — accepted manuscript or published version — under DOE's Public Access Policy.

sources.name: OSTI.GOV Search API
sources.steward: Office of Scientific and Technical Information
sources.scope: DOE's master collection of research results: technical reports, journal articles and accepted manuscripts, conference papers, patents, books and theses, plus metadata for datasets and software held elsewhere.

sources.name: VIPS (DOE patent and software database)
sources.scope: Patents held and software released by the seventeen national laboratories and four NNSA production sites, for technology-transfer lookup: title, abstract, inventors, assignees, first claim, patent status and dates, software type, licences and repository, plus a subject taxonomy and a list of similar records. 15,179 patents and 7,484 software records at the 2026-09-08 count.

sources.name: US Large-Scale Solar Photovoltaic Database (USPVDB)
sources.funder: Office of Critical Materials and Energy Innovation
sources.scope: Locations, array boundaries, and facility attributes (panel technology, axis type, site type, first year of operation, power region) for ground-mounted PV facilities of one megawatt or more.

sources.name: US Wind Turbine Database (USWTDB)
sources.funder: Office of Critical Materials and Energy Innovation
sources.scope: Location, project, and turbine specifications for every utility- scale wind turbine in the United States, land-based and offshore, with FAA identifiers and the project's capacity and year.

sources.name: ALCF computing status
sources.scope: Current status of ALCF systems and their scheduled maintenance, as presented by the facility's own status page.
sources.blocked_reason: Blocked probe. The status page is an Angular application and its data paths return HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare challenge to a scripted client, which under decision 0007 is blocked_probe and NOT gated: a WAF refusing this client shape says nothing about whether the data is public. One real-browser check, watching the application's own network calls, would settle both the endpoint and the posture. Joins the blocked-probe backlog.

sources.name: GAMESS quantum chemistry package
sources.scope: A quantum chemistry program developed at Ames.
sources.blocked_reason: Software distribution, not a data API. Nothing to build; registered for crosswalk truthfulness.

sources.name: Active Thermochemical Tables (ATcT)
sources.scope: Thermochemical values from a self-consistent thermochemical network.
sources.blocked_reason: No API found. A PuRe resource with no machine interface is worth an email.

sources.name: Geospatial Energy Mapper (GEM)
sources.scope: Energy infrastructure siting layers: transmission, generation, environmental constraints.
sources.blocked_reason: Blocked probe. Needs one browser-grade check before its access posture can be recorded.

sources.name: Materials Data Facility
sources.scope: Published materials-science datasets with searchable metadata.
sources.blocked_reason: Phase 4. Needs a globus_search adapter and the credential model extended to Globus tokens, which behave unlike API keys.

sources.name: ARM Data Center (Live data services)
sources.scope: Atmospheric measurements from ARM's fixed and mobile observatories: radiometers, radars, lidars, sondes, and derived value- added products. One of DOE's seven designated PuRe data resources.
sources.blocked_reason: Phase 4. Needs the earth server, the account-token credential path, and the citation block wired end to end.

sources.name: ARPA-E project database
sources.scope: ARPA-E funded projects: programme, performer, award amount, status, technology area.
sources.blocked_reason: Phase 5 and Gate E. The endpoint works today; the posture decision (harvest, do not proxy) is what makes this a scheduled job rather than an adapter.

sources.name: NNDC evaluated nuclear data files
sources.scope: Evaluated nuclear structure and reaction data: ENSDF, ENDF libraries, NuDat.
sources.blocked_reason: Blocked on decision 0011's open sub-question: ingest these bulk files or wrap IAEA's API. Weighted toward ingest because of the snapshot age, and deliberately left to Phase 4.

sources.name: EAGLE-I historical outage datasets
sources.steward: Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response
sources.scope: County-level electricity outage records covering roughly 92% of US customers at 15-minute intervals, released annually.

neighbors.name: EnergyPlus-MCP and OpenStudio-MCP
neighbors.maintainer: LBNL Energy Technologies Area; National Laboratory of the Rockies
neighbors.why_not_absorbed: A different product class. These wrap SIMULATORS — you give them a model and they run it — where DOE-MCP serves published data. Wrapping a simulator means owning its installation, its version compatibility, and its runtime, none of which the provenance envelope has anything useful to say about. The 185 or more combined tools would also breach the sizing ceiling ninefold.

neighbors.name: DOE Genesis Mission MCP deployments (gated)
neighbors.why_not_absorbed: Access-gated by design and pointed at internal instruments, facilities, and compute. Wrapping a gated server would produce a tool that fails for every public user, which is worse than not having it. The named watch items are BNL's PanDA MCP, Argonne's Globus-service MCPs, LBNL's CBorg, and the gated Genesis Skills repository on OSTI's GitLab.
neighbors.install: unavailable — access is gated (OneID / RFA / SSO)

neighbors.name: Materials Project MCP (inside mp-api)
neighbors.maintainer: Materials Project, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory
neighbors.why_not_absorbed: It IS absorbed, which is why this entry exists to say so. Materials Project ships its first-party MCP server inside the `mp-api` Python library (search and fetch shipped as of 0.46.0; fetch_all, fetch_many, phase-diagram lookup and an mpmcp CLI in development). Because the upstream ships a LIBRARY rather than only a server, decision 0011 routes it to depend-and-wrap: declare the dependency, write thin tools over it, and avoid asking a user to install and configure a second MCP server for one domain. The library's surface is reshaped into DOE-MCP's tool contract rather than re-exported, because 0014's sizing bands bind a wrapper like anything else.

neighbors.name: NASA Earthdata (CMR) MCP
neighbors.why_not_absorbed: Another agency's data and another agency's server, already hosted and already working. Rebuilding it would duplicate NASA's own infrastructure to no one's benefit. The overlap with DOE-MCP is narrow and specific — the ORNL DAAC — and there the publisher triple already carries the answer on every provenance entry: ORNL operates it, NASA funds it.
neighbors.install: remote server — configure the endpoint cmr.earthdata.nasa.gov/mcp/v1

neighbors.name: NEPA-MCP
neighbors.why_not_absorbed: Server-only and far too large. 56 tools across 23 servers is more than twice the hard ceiling a single DOE-MCP profile may carry, and its release cadence — every three to six days — would make any wrapper permanently behind. DOE-MCP registers the underlying NEPA document database as a `proposed` manifest that says exactly this, so the registry answers "not a gap, a decision".

known_limitations: A 12-month administrative embargo interval applies before an accepted manuscript appears. Recent DOE-funded work is therefore systematically absent, and an empty result for a 2026 paper means "not yet released", not "does not exist".

A fulltext link is present when `has_fulltext` is true and absent otherwise; the servlet URL pattern resolves for those records only. Constructing one for a record without full text produces a dead link, so the adapter emits only what the API supplies or the manifest templates for records the API marked as having full text.
An index of DOE-funded results, not of all energy research. Absence here says nothing about whether work exists; it says DOE did not fund or receive it.

DOIs arrive as full https://doi.org/ URLs rather than bare DOIs, which breaks naive deduplication against OSTI.GOV records of the same work. The adapter normalizes both to a bare DOI and keeps the URL form as the locator.
ScienceCinema was retired as a standalone product on 2025-09-05 and its ~3,600 multimedia items folded into this collection. Whether they can be isolated by any filter here is unverified.
Sixteen times smaller than OSTI.GOV (260K against 4.38M) by design, not by omission. A literature search that finds nothing here should try OSTI.GOV before concluding anything.

Some records carry future `publication_date` values, which is correct rather than a data error: OSTI accepts scheduled-publication metadata. Sorting by date puts unpublished work first unless a range is set.

`product_type` filters on OSTI's own vocabulary — "Technical Report", "Journal Article" — and the value "Dataset" returns zero here even though datasets exist, because dataset records live in DOE Data Explorer. Checked live 2026-09-02. A caller filtering for datasets on this API gets an empty result that means "wrong API", not "none".

examples.why: Every wind turbine the USGS/LBNL inventory places in Rhode Island, five to a page, with the publisher's own count and the confidence codes on each row.

data.units: t_cap is one turbine's rated capacity in kilowatts and p_cap is the whole project's capacity in megawatts, which are different units on adjacent columns. Hub height (t_hh), rotor diameter (t_rd) and total height to blade tip (t_ttlh) are metres; rotor swept area (t_rsa) is square metres; xlong and ylat are decimal degrees.
data.confidence_codes: t_conf_loc and t_conf_atr both run 1 to 3, and 3 is the confident case. Location: 1 means no turbine was visible in the image, 2 a pad or parts on the ground, 3 an installed turbine. Attributes: 1 means nothing beyond total height and year, 2 incomplete or conflicting sources, 3 complete and consistent across sources. t_img_date is the date of the image the location was checked against, and t_img_src names the imagery.
data.note: An inventory of individual wind turbines: where they are and what they are, one row each, not how much they generated. For output, capacity factors, or anything hourly, use energy.get_data against EIA — the eia_id column on these rows is EIA's own plant id and is how the two line up. The API states no release version of its own, so dataset_version is this registry's record of the current release, checked 2026-09-08.
data.more: 35 records match. Page with offset to read past the 5 returned here rather than describing these as all of them.

warnings.message: 1 of the 5 records returned carry a confidence code below the publisher's top score, which means the compilers could not fully confirm the location or the attributes from imagery and records. Those rows are estimates and are marked as such in the data; reporting them beside the confirmed ones without the distinction turns an estimate into a survey. The codes are decoded in confidence_codes.

data.calendar: Daymet's year is always 365 days. 29 February is present and 31 December is dropped in leap years, so an annual total from a leap year is a 365-day total and the missing date is named on any answer whose range covers it.
data.note: Daily modelled surface weather for the 1 km cell holding this point. Precipitation is a daily total; tmax and tmin are daily extremes, so a daily mean has to be computed and is not published. For observations at a station rather than a modelled grid cell, this is the wrong source.

warnings.message: Values are modelled estimates for the 1 km cell containing the point, interpolated from ground stations. They are not a station observation and the service reports no cell centre, so a value here is the model's account of that kilometre rather than a measurement at the coordinates given.

examples.why: Computed structures containing gallium and nitrogen from the Materials Project's OPTIMADE endpoint, marked as computed rather than measured.

data.coverage_note: This keyless route serves structures and formulas. The Materials Project's electronic structure, phase diagrams, elastic tensors and the rest are behind its own keyed API and the mp-api library, which is a separate source in this registry. A caller reading "Materials Project" will assume the whole database; this route is one part of it.
data.federation_note: This is one provider in the OPTIMADE federation, and the DOE member of it. A material absent here may exist at another provider; that is a different answer from its not existing.
data.note: Crystal structures matching the filter. `filter` takes the OPTIMADE grammar directly through filter_expression, and the named arguments build one for the common cases; call materials.describe_structure_fields for the properties this provider allows and for its own extension fields.

known_limitations: Computed, not measured. A Materials Project structure is a calculation's output under a stated functional, and treating it as an experimental crystal structure is a category error.
This route is narrower than the publisher's own API. Structures and formulas are here; energetics beyond the stability block, electronic structure, and phase diagrams are behind the keyed route.
OPTIMADE is a federation standard with 29 providers, of which this is the DOE member. A structure absent here may well exist at another provider, and that is a different answer from its not existing.
The provider extension fields are not portable. `_mp_stability` means what the Materials Project says it means and has no counterpart at another provider.

warnings.message: These are computed structures, not measured ones: each is a calculation's output under a stated functional. Reporting one as an experimentally determined crystal structure is a category error.
